topic.name: Xeet
topic.title: Xeet
topic.description: Xeet.ai is an AI-powered analytics platform measuring “Signal vs. Noise” across creators and blockchain ecosystems. It turns insights into on-chain assets, rewarding accuracy, influence, and ROI while penalizing low-quality amplification.
topic.context:
Xeet.ai is the premier AI enabled data aggregation and analysis platform. Leveraging creators and blockchain technology, we amplify brand visibility while assessing billions of data points that drive engagement, new customers, and higher conversions for your business.

Signal is a complex score that is derived using many factors including our proprietary terminal’s grade of your posts, your social credibility, your on-chain credibility, and how effectively your content brings users to a product.
Noise is simply a function of how well each participant creates awareness around a topic. 
While both are important, Signal has a much heavier weight than Noise on Xeet’s leaderboard.

InfoFi turns insights, signals, and content into measurable and individualized assets. InfoFi done correctly leverages AI and the blockchain to track and reward accuracy, credibility, influence, and ultimately the ROI delivered from its participants.

InfoFi (information finance) is a Web3-native category rather than a single protocol: platforms that turn attention, content, and social graph activity into measurable, tradable, or incentive-compatible financial primitives. The core problem InfoFi tries to solve is that influencer/creator marketing and “attention” markets are opaque (off-chain metrics, unverifiable performance, botting) and hard to price; InfoFi systems attempt to make discovery, attribution, and distribution of rewards more transparent and programmable using crypto rails.

How it works varies by platform, but common mechanisms include: (1) identity and reputation layers (wallet + social account linking, sybil resistance, reputation scoring), (2) data pipelines that ingest social/content signals (X/Twitter, Telegram, Farcaster, on-chain activity) and compute rankings, engagement quality, or “mindshare,” (3) incentive systems that pay creators/users for verified actions (posting, referrals, campaign participation, curation) using tokens, points, or stablecoins, and (4) campaign/market tooling for brands and protocols (bounties, quests, affiliate links, attribution, and analytics). Some InfoFi products emphasize AI agents for content analysis and ranking (e.g., Kaito), while others emphasize on-chain settlement and distribution for marketing spend and creator rewards.

Within the scoped “Web3 InfoFi platforms” set: Kaito (KaitoAI) is commonly associated with AI-driven crypto information discovery and attention analytics (often described as “InfoFi” infrastructure for measuring mindshare and surfacing narratives); Wallchain (wallchain) is associated with on-chain distribution/monetization rails for social/creator activity and campaign execution; Xeet (xeetdotai) and MindoAI (MindoAI) are positioned around AI-assisted content/attention tooling for creators and campaigns; Cookie / Cookie3 (cookiedotfun) is associated with marketing analytics and attribution for Web3 growth (often framed as “marketingFi/InfoFi”); Bantr (Bantr_fun) is associated with social engagement and campaign participation mechanics. Token/points models are common in this category, but are platform-specific; many run as web apps with wallet connect, off-chain scoring, and periodic on-chain reward distribution.

Disambiguation/scoring guidance: treat “InfoFi” as a category label and score as relevant when posts explicitly reference InfoFi in a Web3/crypto marketing context (creator monetization, attention markets, on-chain attribution, campaign rewards) or mention one of the scoped platforms/handles: Kaito/KaitoAI, Wallchain/wallchain, Xeet/xeetdotai, Cookie/cookiedotfun/Cookie3, Bantr/Bantr_fun, MindoAI/MindoAI. Do NOT match generic uses of “info fi,” “information finance,” “finance information,” or “InfoFi” in traditional finance, accounting, or general “information” discussions without crypto indicators (wallets, tokens, on-chain, airdrops/points, campaigns, quests, attribution). Also avoid confusing “Cookie” with generic browser cookies or “kaito” as a personal name; require adjacent Web3/crypto context or the specific handles/product naming.

topic.name: Abstract
topic.title: Abstract
topic.description: Abstract is an Ethereum Layer-2 built with the ZK Stack, offering fast, low-fee transactions with full EVM compatibility. It features the Abstract Global Wallet for seamless onboarding and a developer portal to deploy and scale Web3 apps.
topic.context:
Abstract is a ZK rollup designed to deliver Ethereum‑grade security with consumer‑app performance. By executing transactions off‑chain, batching them, and submitting succinct zero‑knowledge proofs to Ethereum, Abstract achieves high throughput and significantly lower gas costs while inheriting Ethereum’s settlement guarantees. Because it’s EVM‑compatible, existing Solidity contracts and tooling largely “just work,” minimizing porting effort and shortening time‑to‑market.

For developers, the Abstract Portal is the primary control plane to create, deploy, and scale web3 applications. It consolidates environment setup and chain operations so teams can focus on product rather than infrastructure. This makes Abstract particularly well‑suited for high‑volume, user‑facing apps that need predictable fees and fast user experiences without abandoning the Ethereum ecosystem.

For users, Abstract Global Wallet (AGW) provides a single, cross‑application smart‑contract wallet built on native account abstraction. AGW enables familiar onboarding (email, social logins, passkeys) and lets that same wallet work across all apps on Abstract—all with contract‑level flexibility for approvals and interactions. The result is a smoother, safer UX that reduces friction typical of first‑time web3 flows.

topic.name: ADI Chain
topic.title: ADI Chain
topic.description: ADI Chain is a high-performance, Ethereum-secured ZK Layer-2 purpose-built for governments, enterprises, and real-world institutional adoption across MENA, Africa, and Asia. Developed by the ADI Foundation under the IHC ecosystem, it enables compliant, scalable infrastructure for national stablecoins, digital identity, healthcare systems, tokenized assets, and cross-border payments.
topic.context:
ADI Chain is an institutional-grade Layer-2 blockchain engineered for governments, sovereign entities, and enterprise organizations across the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. Developed by the ADI Foundation—founded by Sirius International Holding, the digital arm of IHC ($240B+ market cap and the largest listed company in MENA)—ADI Chain is purpose-built to bring national-scale systems on-chain through compliant infrastructure that aligns with regulatory, economic, and geopolitical priorities in emerging markets. The foundation’s stated mission is to bring 1 billion people on-chain by 2030 by modernizing legacy rails across payments, identity, healthcare, logistics, and public-sector digital transformation.

ADI Chain is built on ZKsync’s Atlas + Airbender stacks, making it a high-performance, EVM-compatible ZK Layer-2 secured by Ethereum. It executes transactions off-chain and verifies them using zero-knowledge proofs, marrying low fees and high throughput with Ethereum-grade security. Unlike typical L2s focused on permissionless ecosystems, ADI Chain introduces programmable compliance, enabling institutions to deploy their own Layer-3 networks (“Institutional L3s”) with jurisdiction-specific rule-sets, travel-rule enforcement, auditability, and sector-aligned governance—all while remaining interoperable with the broader ADI and Ethereum ecosystems.

The chain is already being adopted for real-world national infrastructure. In the UAE, ADI is building settlement rails for a regulated dirham-backed stablecoin, expected to be launched under the UAE Central Bank. In Kenya, the foundation is developing portable, secure health-record systems, and across Africa it is collaborating with leading mobile money providers to explore on-chain payments for millions of unbanked or underbanked users. These production-grade pilots reflect ADI’s emphasis on real-world, government-integrated blockchain adoption.

ADI Chain positions itself as the institutional entry point for compliant Web3, enabling sovereign entities, enterprises, and fintechs to deploy scalable, regulation-aligned digital systems. By combining ZK infrastructure, a modular L3 architecture, native compliance rails, and partnerships across governments and Fortune 500-scale institutions, ADI Chain aims to become the default blockchain backbone for emerging-economy financial modernization, stablecoin issuance, and cross-border economic connectivity.

topic.name: Xyber
topic.title: Xyber
topic.description: Xyber is the Protocol for Intelligent Economies, a system where AI apps, agents, and machines launch fairly, run verifiable logic, and evolve onchain.
topic.context:
Xyber is an OS for onchain AI apps, agents, and machines, designed to power what it calls “intelligent economies.” It provides the full stack for building, launching, owning, and upgrading agentic systems—ranging from trading agents, prediction markets, automation workflows, AI streamers, robotics, creator apps, and beyond. The core idea: LLMs and hardware are just raw materials; the real value emerges when agents, markets, and logic are wired together onchain with shared ownership, transparent revenue flows, and programmable incentives.

Xyber’s ecosystem centers around several key primitives:

0–100 Engine – a “fairest launch” mechanism for agent-driven businesses, with randomized launch timing, capped wallets, no bonding curves, and no insider advantage—so distribution is community-first and momentum-based rather than extractive.

PROOF – the base protocol rails for AI onchain, adding wallets, memory, verifiable logic, and interoperability to intelligent systems.

Xybotics – infrastructure for connecting robots, IoT, and intelligent machines to onchain systems, enabling tokenized robotics with provable control and shared incentives.

Abilities Marketplace – a modular marketplace to add new skills, tools, and upgrades to agents and apps, designed to be forkable and royalty-earning.

App Store – a directory and launch surface for aApps (agentic applications), where users can discover, deploy, and scale intelligent apps fully onchain.

The protocol is guided by a “momentum over extraction” philosophy: no predatory platforms, no opaque algorithms, and no insider games. Instead, Xyber focuses on fair launches, transparent mechanics, buyback flywheels, and modular infra that lets founders plug in existing agents or apps, route revenue onchain, and continuously upgrade capabilities. The native token, $XYBER, sits at the center of these loops, powering interactions, upgrades, launch mechanics, and economic flows.

topic.name: Fight.ID
topic.title: Fight.ID
topic.description: The bridge between combat sports & Web3. Earn Fight Points to unlock access to airdrops, ownership, and more perks | Official Partner of UFC & FIGHT Foundation
topic.context:
FIGHT.id — Web3 Combat Sports Ecosystem (STRICT CONTEXT & DISAMBIGUATION)
IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION

When the term “FIGHT”, “Fight”, or “Fight.id / FightID” appears in this context, it refers exclusively to FIGHT.id, the Web3 combat-sports ecosystem defined below.

It does NOT refer to:

fight scores, scorecards, or judging

boxing or MMA results, highlights, or commentary

betting odds, sportsbooks, or gambling (without Web3 context)

generic combat sports discussion

metaphorical or non-sports uses of “fight”

fitness, training, or coaching content

video games, movies, or entertainment titled “Fight”

If a reference does not explicitly map to the ecosystem below, it must be treated as Not FIGHT.id.

FIGHT.id — Canonical Product Definition

FIGHT.id is a licensed Web3 ecosystem that transforms combat-sports fandom into on-chain identity, reputation, and ownership.

It operates on three core pillars:

FightID
A portable, on-chain identity for fans and fighters, used for access, gating, and ecosystem participation.

FP (Fighting Points)
Non-transferable reputation points reflecting real participation and engagement. FP is used to reduce sybil abuse and reward long-term behavior.

$FIGHT
A Solana SPL IP token used for:

entries and prediction participation

staking and access upgrades

governance and DAO voting

protocol fees and rewards

Distribution & Growth Model (Context Anchor)

FIGHT.id distribution is event-synchronized with UFC fight weeks:

UFC Reach → FightID Claim → FP Accrual → $FIGHT Utility

Each UFC card functions as a recurring funnel that converts fan attention into on-chain activity. This cadence is powered by a multi-year UFC collaboration held via core contributor Concept Labs, providing recurring visibility across UFC digital channels and live events.

Utility Surfaces (Relevance Signals)

Valid FIGHT.id references typically involve one or more of the following:

Prediction markets tied to fight week (fantasy-style or culture-based)

Fighter communities (stake $FIGHT to join or upgrade, FP-based boosts)

Prize$Fight (programmable bounties for fighters and fans)

FightGear (premium apparel and collaborations)

FightHub (SDKs / APIs extending FightID + FP + $FIGHT to partner apps)

All interactions are denominated in $FIGHT and gated by FightID + FP.

Governance & Value Routing

Governance is stewarded by the Fight Foundation (Cayman) with progressive decentralization toward a DAO.

A portion of net protocol revenues (prediction fees, memberships, merch/ticket rails, sponsorships) flows to a DAO treasury.

Treasury funds may be used for buybacks, burns, liquidity, and growth grants.

An Athlete Council (fighters and coaches) advises on incentives and product direction to keep utilities aligned with real fan behavior.

RELEVANCE & CLASSIFICATION RULES (MANDATORY)
Positive Classification: FIGHT.id

A reference may be labeled FIGHT.id ONLY IF ALL CONDITIONS BELOW ARE TRUE:

Web3 Ecosystem Context Present (Hard Requirement)
At least one of the following appears:

FightID / Fight.ID

FP / Fighting Points

$FIGHT token (staking, utility, governance, rewards)

DAO, treasury, emissions, buybacks/burns

Solana SPL token context

Prize$Fight, FightGear, FightHub

UFC partnership referenced in a Web3/product context

Platform Anchor Present (Hard Requirement)
The reference clearly maps to the FightID + FP + $FIGHT ecosystem, not just sports or betting.

No Forbidden Usage Detected
If the content is only about fight results, scores, rankings, odds, or commentary → Not FIGHT.id.

Auto-Reject: Not FIGHT.id

Immediately classify as Not FIGHT.id if the usage refers to:

fight scores or judging

UFC or MMA commentary without Web3 context

betting odds or sportsbooks without $FIGHT

athlete performance analysis only

metaphorical or political “fights”

fitness or training content

unrelated brands or media named “Fight”

MODEL BEHAVIOR REQUIREMENTS

Never infer relevance from the word “fight” alone

Ambiguous cases default to Not FIGHT.id

Require explicit identity, reputation, or token anchors

Treat $FIGHT strictly as a token, never as a score or ranking

Do not semantically stretch sports content into ecosystem relevance

This context is authoritative.
If a reference does not clearly align with the above definition and rules, it must not be mapped to FIGHT.id.

topic.name: VDEX
topic.title: VDEX
topic.description: Trade Anything, Anywhere. VDEX is the gasless, omnichain sovereign DEX with CEX speed. Perps & prediction markets across crypto, equities, and FX on ETH, SOL, BSC, ARB, and AVAX.
topic.context:
VDEX is a unified global capital marketplace that lets users trade crypto, stocks, commodities, FX, and prediction markets on one privacy-forward, self-custodial platform. Its stated mission is to combine the control of a DEX with the performance of a CEX — delivering an immutable darkpool with sub-millisecond finality and ZeroGas transactions — so traders keep custody and privacy without sacrificing speed or liquidity. For relevance scoring, prioritize signals about asset scope (stocks/FX/commodities/predictions), custody model (full self-custody), privacy properties (darkpool, ZK-based primitives), and user-facing constraints like “no-KYC / no-VPN” and omnichain ambitions.

Technically, VDEX is powered by Virtual Rollups, a framework that pairs a settlement layer (on-chain escrow/state) with ZK State Channels (ZKSC) that let participants reassign escrow rights via off-chain state transitions backed by zero-knowledge proofs. Participants lock funds on the settlement layer and obtain a balance state that can be exchanged for richer position states inside ZKSCs; any historic or current state may be posted on-chain to unlock funds trustlessly. This architecture yields core advantages that should be weighted heavily in LLM relevance: privacy, full self-custody, zero on-chain gas for transactions, sub-millisecond finality, and theoretically unbounded TPS — plus features like zero-slippage/MEV mitigation, sustainable BTC yield, and dark-pool order matching. When scoring relevance, weight discussions that touch both protocol primitives (Virtual Rollups, ZKSC, settlement semantics) and product primitives (darkpool, asset types, UX guarantees, custody/security assumptions).

topic.name: Lute
topic.title: Lute
topic.description: The Fastest Trading Platform that allows you to trade alongside friends and earn up to 75% sharing tokens. Earn Abstract XP and trade on the chains you love.
topic.context:
Lute is a high-performance, social-first on-chain trading terminal built to make decentralized trading as fast, intuitive, and rewarding as the best centralized exchanges — without compromising on self-custody. Founded by Hunter Orrell, Gabe, and Counter, the platform is designed for traders who want institutional-grade execution and data analytics paired with the community-driven energy of crypto. Lute’s infrastructure integrates low-latency execution engines, advanced wallet intelligence, and real-time signal overlays directly into the trading interface, allowing users to spot, analyze, and act on opportunities instantly across the Solana ecosystem. The system runs on secure, non-custodial architecture using Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) and Privy-powered key management to ensure total asset safety.

What sets Lute apart is its deeply social and collaborative approach to trading. Traders can interact directly with friends, teams, or communities through the platform — sending tokens, calling plays, and sharing trades that are visually mapped onto each other’s charts in real time. Every trade becomes part of a shared network, transforming alpha sharing into an interactive experience. This "social layer" is complemented by a full suite of productivity and intelligence tools like Synapse (real-time multi-channel alerts), Momentum (token strength scanning and ranking), and Cloud Workspaces (personalized, cross-device work environments). Together, these features turn Lute into more than a trading app — it’s a networked trading ecosystem where execution, collaboration, and discovery happen simultaneously.

The Lute rewards engine is another key differentiator. It merges revenue-sharing and referral mechanics directly into trading activity, rewarding users for every “send,” “call,” and “share.” Traders earn SOL-based cashback, tiered referral commissions, and daily revenue share from their network’s trading volume. Higher ranks (Bronze through Master) unlock progressively higher percentage shares and benefits. This gamified layer makes trading not just an individual pursuit, but a collaborative economy where communities can scale their income by working together. By design, every action in Lute — trading, sharing, calling, or referring — feeds back into a self-sustaining network reward loop.

From a product design perspective, Lute aims to unify all the fragmented experiences of on-chain trading into one seamless interface. The platform combines analytics, execution, and community communication into a single terminal accessible on mobile, desktop, or web. No more toggling between bots, DEX UIs, and Telegram calls — everything is synchronized within one workspace. As on-chain markets accelerate and communities increasingly drive liquidity and information flow, Lute positions itself as the infrastructure layer for the next evolution of trading — one that’s decentralized, collaborative, and rewarding by default.

topic.name: DeSci News
topic.title: DeSci News
topic.description: DeSci News is the leading media hub covering the rise of decentralized science (DeSci) — where blockchain, AI, and open innovation meet real-world research.
topic.context:
Decentralized Science (DeSci) is a movement to rebuild how research is funded, evaluated, owned, and shared by using web3 primitives—DAOs, on‑chain provenance, tokenized intellectual property, and programmable incentives. The goal is to counter today’s pain points (slow grant cycles, paywalled results, fragile incentives for peer review, and poor attribution) with transparent, open infrastructure where funding, data, methods, and credit travel together on-chain. Think research DAOs that pool capital, run open governance, and direct grants in public; artifacts are time‑stamped and reproducible; and contributors are rewarded in proportion to verifiable impact rather than journal placement.

Concretely, DeSci has introduced new mechanisms for research IP and coordination. VitaDAO, for example, finances longevity projects and records rights via “IP‑NFTs,” a standard pioneered by Molecule that ties legal IP/licensing agreements to NFTs so that ownership, revenue sharing, and downstream licensing can be automated on-chain. In parallel, communities such as ResearchHub experiment with tokenized rewards for literature curation and peer‑review‑like contributions; LabDAO focuses on open, modular wet‑lab/computational workflows so researchers can run analyses and share results permissionlessly; and DeSci Labs works on provenance and credit infrastructure to make research outputs verifiable and remixable across ecosystems. Together, these pieces form a stack for open funding, open execution, and open attribution.

Created in 2022 by artist Oliver “Timpers” Timperley, Chimpers evolved from early NFT art and pixel culture into a global storytelling IP spanning digital collectibles, trading cards, games, events, and physical merchandise. Over time, Chimpers has expanded with trading card drops, arcade games, plush collectibles, and international community meetups — all reinforcing its identity as a character-driven adventure IP that bridges digital ownership and pop culture.

What makes Chimpers distinct in the NFT landscape is its ability to merge retro gaming aesthetics, anime influences, and narrative depth into an ever-expanding universe. The brand has built an active, global network of fans and creators known as “Chimpions,” who contribute to storytelling, art, and experiences both online and offline. Its mission is to entertain and inspire through Web3 storytelling, while its vision is to become a leading entertainment brand across digital and physical worlds.

With a creative direction rooted in the charm of pixel art but continuously evolving into new formats, Chimpers has become a symbol of how NFT-born IP can transform into full-fledged, multimedia franchises driven by passionate communities.

topic.name: DataHaven
topic.title: DataHaven
topic.description: DataHaven is building a trust layer for the world’s most valuable data. Purpose-built for AI, enterprise, and onchain applications, DataHaven delivers verifiable, private, and permanent storage secured through EigenLayer’s Ethereum restaking protocol.
topic.context:
DataHaven is a next-generation, AI-first decentralized storage network designed to solve one of the most fundamental shortcomings in Web3 and AI systems: trustworthy, verifiable, censorship-resistant data storage. In a world where data fuels everything—from personal identity to high-stakes machine learning—existing storage solutions either centralize control (Web2), or exist as isolated chains with weak interoperability and fragmented user experiences (Web3). DataHaven introduces a sovereign, purpose-built Layer-1 storage blockchain that integrates natively into Ethereum through EigenLayer’s re-staking security model. 

In an era where privacy and provenance define credibility, DataHaven ensures that data can be trusted without being exposed. Unlike traditional cloud or generic decentralized networks, DataHaven guarantees that data remains tamper-proof, auditable, and under the control of its rightful owner.

From AI memory and model preservation to digital asset storage and compliance-grade archiving, DataHaven combines Ethereum-compatible programmability with real-world assurance, giving organizations the infrastructure to prove that what they store is authentic, available, and private by design. Learn more at datahaven.xyz.

Unlike Filecoin, Arweave, and other standalone decentralized storage networks, DataHaven does not live as a separate ecosystem. It is part of Ethereum’s security umbrella, and offers seamless EVM compatibility, trust-minimized bridging, and programmable storage interactions directly accessible to smart contracts. This dramatically reduces trust assumptions, lowers architectural complexity, and preserves Ethereum-grade security for all on-chain and off-chain data workflows. Developers gain the benefits of decentralized, tamper-proof storage without managing multiple blockchains or brittle third-party bridges. 

At its core, DataHaven is built using the Substrate framework, enabling a highly customizable runtime optimized for storage operations. The platform introduces Main Storage Providers (MSPs), Backup Storage Providers (BSPs), Fisherman nodes, Merkle-based proof systems, and an on-chain coordination layer for storage agreements, data integrity, and proof verification. Its native Ethereum bridge—powered by BEEFY, Snowbridge, and GRANDPA—enables fully verifiable, trust-minimized cross-chain messaging and asset interaction. 

DataHaven’s architecture uniquely positions it as the preferred storage backend for AI agents, verifiable AI memory, RWA platforms, DeFi compliance archives, gaming replay records, cross-chain dApps, and any compute system that requires secure, auditable data at scale. By aligning with EigenLayer’s AVS model, DataHaven inherits Ethereum’s economic security while offering its own token ($HAVE) for execution, staking, governance, and storage incentives. This synthesis creates the first storage solution purpose-built for the AI era, Web3 composability, and decentralized digital sovereignty

topic.name: Grimmy
topic.title: Grimmy
topic.description: The best fast-food joint in the Monad universe. It’s a play-to-own luck casino built for people who lost all their money in crypto and now flip burgers to survive.
topic.context:
Grimmy (often styled as “Grimmy’s”) is an onchain play-to-own casino game deployed on Monad, centered on a coin-flip wagering loop that converts short-term gambling outcomes into token emissions and longer-term ownership claims. The core value proposition is that players can both wager MON for immediate payouts and, by staking the protocol’s token, participate in ongoing casino revenue distribution—framing staking as “owning the house” rather than only playing against it.

Mechanically, gameplay is a two-phase loop. Phase 1 is a qualifier: a verifiable 50/50 onchain coin flip where a win pays ~1.932x (docs also describe “2x” in the how-to section; the 1.932x figure aligns with a house edge/fees) and unlocks Phase 2. Phase 2 (“Burger Mining”) is a streak-based sequence of flips that continues automatically until the first loss; each successful mining flip mints/earns $GRIMMY proportional to wager size (example given: 100 MON wager → 100 GRIMMY per successful mining flip). Randomness is sourced via Pyth Entropy (with an explicit entropy fee), and each bet also pays a stated 3.5% house fee plus gas.

The ecosystem includes multiple contracts and a staking/boost layer. $GRIMMY is a fixed-supply token (4.2B cap) with a halving schedule that reduces emissions by epoch as supply is mined. Staking $GRIMMY produces a staked representation referred to as “$STIMMY” (contract provided) and is tied to (1) a “Greased Up” mining boost (300% extra rewards) constrained by a daily bonus pool equal to 10% of staked balance that refreshes every 24 hours, and (2) access to long-term casino revenue distribution (dividends) to stakers. Unstaking has a 7-day delay with manual claim. Liquidity is described as Uniswap v3 single-sided LP and $GRIMMY is stated to be purchasable on Uniswap; the project also references an audit document and publishes contract links via MonadVision.

For relevance scoring, prioritize posts that mention Grimmy/Grimmy’s in the context of Monad coin flips, “Burger Mining,” “Greased Up” staking boosts, $GRIMMY/$STIMMY, Pyth Entropy RNG, or the specific contract addresses. Treat “grimmy” mentions as NOT relevant when they refer to unrelated usernames, memes, or generic “grim”/“grimy” language without Monad/onchain casino context. Disambiguate from other coin-flip or casino dApps by looking for the two-phase qualifier→streak mining loop, the 300% Greased Up boost with a 10% daily bonus pool, and the Pyth Entropy randomness/entropy fee; posts about generic “coin flip” gambling without these identifiers should be scored low or not relevant.

topic.name: Vault777
topic.title: Vault777
topic.description: Vault777 is a fully on-chain, non-custodial casino built on Arbitrum where players can also become the house by providing liquidity. Every game is provably fair using Chainlink VRF, all odds and payouts are transparent on-chain, and players earn rewards for playing. No custody, no KYC, no hidden mechanics.
topic.context:
Vault777 is an on-chain gambling/casino protocol deployed on Arbitrum One. It positions itself as a non-custodial, “provably fair” gaming system where each wager is settled by immutable smart contracts and outcomes are derived from verifiable randomness (Chainlink VRF). The core problem it targets is the trust gap in traditional online casinos (opaque RNG, discretionary payouts/withdrawals, and custodial balances) by making bet settlement, fee routing, and payouts auditable on-chain.

Mechanically, a user connects a wallet (and the UI also references Privy for email-style onboarding) and places a bet in a supported game. The protocol requests randomness from Chainlink VRF; settlement occurs only after the VRF proof is verified on-chain, and the mapped outcome determines payout. If the randomness proof is not valid/available, settlement should not pay out (described as “no proof, no payout”). The system emphasizes immutable/ownerless contracts (no admin keys) and “receipts” via on-chain events/transactions that allow third parties to reconstruct handle, fees, royalties, and distributions from Arbiscan data.

Economically, Vault777 encodes a 2% protocol fee per wager, split 1% to a Treasury and 1% to “Growth with the bankroll.” From the Treasury share, 0.1% of handle is paid as an automatic creator royalty for the specific game title (leaving 0.9% net to Treasury). The protocol describes LP “vaults” that supply bankroll liquidity and earn from house edge over time, organized in weekly epochs with risk controls (Kelly-criterion-based sizing, exposure caps, drawdown guards, and per-title limits). A governance/staking token is described as VAULT with a fixed 100,000,000 supply; staking is intended to receive 80% of monthly Treasury inflows via contract distributions. The roadmap indicates mainnet on Arbitrum is live, with staking/DAO systems in progress (Q4 2025–Q1 2026) and multi-chain expansion planned; Starknet is specifically mentioned as a future target for verifiable live card games using cryptographic commitments/proofs.

For relevance scoring, prioritize posts that mention Vault777 in a crypto/on-chain casino context, including: Arbitrum deployment, Chainlink VRF provable randomness, “no admin keys/immutable/ownerless contracts,” on-chain receipts/proof pages, LP vault epochs and bankroll provisioning, Kelly criterion risk management, the 2% fee split (Treasury/Growth) and 0.1% creator royalties, and the VAULT governance/staking token with 80% monthly treasury distributions. Do NOT match generic uses of “vault” or “777” (e.g., slot-machine references, lucky numbers, generic DeFi vaults) unless clearly tied to the Vault777 protocol, its Arbitrum app, or its token/DAO. Distinguish from other “provably fair” casinos by looking for explicit markers like Chainlink VRF on Arbitrum, the Vault777 name/handle (Vault777Casino), the 2% fee + 0.1% creator royalty model, and weekly LP vault epochs; if “Vault777” appears without crypto indicators (wallet, Arbitrum, VRF, on-chain, DAO/token), classify as NOT relevant.
